answer.policy_title: 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review — Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines; Lumbar Spine Surgery (Evolent Clinical Guideline 1760)
answer.effective_date: Effective July 1, 2026 through July 1, 2027; the document identifies a last revision date of December 2025 and an implementation date of July 2026.
criteria_quotes: All appropriate supporting documentation, including recent pertinent office visit notes, laboratory data, and results of any special testing must be provided.
In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery.
Operative treatment is indicated only when the natural history of surgically treated lesions is better than the natural history for non-operatively treated lesions.
All operative interventions must be based on a positive correlation with clinical findings, the natural history of the disease, the clinical course, and diagnostic tests or imaging results.
answer.appeal_deadline: February 6, 2027. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received within 180 days of August 10, 2026.

submission_route.mail: Ambetter Attn: Appeals and Grievances Department, P.O. Box 10341, Van Nuys, CA 91410
submission_route.recommended_submission: Submit a written appeal with the denial notice, reference number POC-4825AA1F8B-42990, the requested CPT 63030, the surgeon's operative plan, relevant office notes, imaging reports and images if available, neurologic examination findings, diagnosis, treatment history, and documentation addressing the applicable conservative-treatment and imaging requirements. Keep proof of fax transmission or certified-mail delivery.

answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The Oklahoma Ambetter clinical-policy page states that Ambetter of Oklahoma uses its own clinical policies, InterQual criteria when no Ambetter clinical policy exists, and delegated-vendor guidelines when utilization management has been delegated. The 2026 provider manual identifies Evolent musculoskeletal care management for spine surgery, and the Evolent guideline specifically includes CPT 63030 under lumbar microdiscectomy. Ask Ambetter Member Services and the provider who submitted the authorization to provide the exact lumbar-spine guideline version used for reference POC-4825AA1F8B-42990, the specific criteria or checklist applied, and the clinical information found missing. Request that this information be supplied in writing as part of the appeal record.
notes: The publicly available Evolent guideline is the best code-specific match located: its lumbar-spine section covers lumbar microdiscectomy and CPT 63030, and it is effective during the date of the denial.

The denial letter itself does not identify Evolent, the guideline number, or the exact subsection applied. Oklahoma Ambetter's public policy page confirms that delegated-vendor guidelines may be used, but the letter does not establish conclusively which criteria reviewer used.

Ambetter's separate public Centene policy titled 'Disc Decompression Procedures' is policy CP.MP.114, but its publicly listed CPT tables do not list CPT 63030. Therefore it should not be treated as the governing code-specific policy for this denial without confirmation from Ambetter.

The public Oklahoma Ambetter page lists CP.MP.114 but does not provide a separate Oklahoma-hosted PDF URL for the Evolent lumbar criteria. The Evolent guideline URL above is the publicly retrieved source.

It frequently involves a laminectomy (removal of the vertebral lamina to relieve pressure on nerve roots). Microdiscectomy (MD) is a refinement of open discectomy and involves a smaller incision in the back, with visualization through an operating microscope. This may include a laminotomy or hemilaminectomy in order to adequately visualize the disc, followed by removal of the disc fragment compressing the affected nerve or nerves. Minimally i nvasive discectomy (MID) techniques include percutaneous manual nucleotomy, automated percutaneous lumbar discectomy, laser discectomy, endoscopic discectomy, microendoscopic discectomy, coblation nucleoplasty, and the disc DeKompressor. Tubular or trochar discectomy is a less invasive technique in which a tubular retractor is inserted over a guidewire, gaining access to the disc by muscle splitting rather than muscle incision and detachment. • • MID procedures involve smaller incisions and surgery with the aid of indirect visualization. Some te chniques employ lasers to vaporize parts of the disc or automated techniques for removing portions of the disc. They include but are not limited to policies relating to evolving medical technologies and procedures, as well as pharmacy policies. Clinical policies help identify whether services are medically necessary based on information found in generally accepted standards of medical practice; peer-reviewed medical literature; government agency/program approval status; evidence-based guidelines and positions of leading national health professional organizations; views of physicians practicing in relevant clinical areas affected by the policy; and other available clinical information. All policies found in the Ambetter of Oklahoma Clinical Policy Manual apply to Ambetter of Oklahoma members. Policies in the Ambetter of Oklahoma Clinical Policy Manual may have either a Ambetter of Oklahoma or a “Centene” heading. Ambetter of Oklahoma utilizes InterQual® criteria for those medical technologies, procedures or pharmaceutical treatments for which a Ambetter of Oklahoma clinical policy does not exist. InterQual is a nationally recognized evidence-based decision support tool. You may access the InterQual® SmartSheet(s)™ for Adult and Pediatric procedures, durable medical equipment and imaging procedures by logging into the secure provider portal or by calling Ambetter of Oklahoma. In addition, Ambetter of Oklahoma may from time to time delegate utilization management of specific services; in such circumstances, the delegated vendor’s guidelines may also be used to support medical necessity and other coverage determinations. Other non-clinical policies (e.g., payment policies) or contract terms may further determine whether a technology, procedure or treatment that is not addressed in the Clinical Policy Manuals or InterQual®criteria is payable by Ambetter of Oklahoma. If you have any questions regarding these policies, please contact Member Services and ask to be directed to the Medical Management department.
